title: Nebuchadnezzar II
summary: King of Babylon who destroyed Jerusalem and the temple.
description: Added from the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)). Dates are those printed in the cited Generations books; no tier 1–4 chronology covers this person.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year.

standby.note: Standby placement only. Generations curriculum (Swanson et al.) prints this BC/AD year on the death entry (562 BC). It is not a sort year. No Anno Mundi, regnal length, or Julian Period figure was converted to obtain it.

birth.note: pending CFAH reference (the CFAH series does not cover this period; no tier 1–4 date exists)

death.note: pending CFAH reference (the CFAH series does not cover this period; no tier 1–4 date exists)

death.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 11 "Babylon Has Fallen (626–539 BC)", PDF p. 343 (printed p. 342)
death.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "562 BC" (PDF p. 497): the same date.

death.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 19 "Babylon Has Fallen", PDF p. 497 (printed p. 483)

reign.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 789b
reign.note: Year cell "4089 3407 414". The third printed figure 414 is the column "Temple", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 44 at the end of the name is the reign length he prints. The end year is not printed on this row.

reign.date: A. M. 3426, when Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylon, and about one hundred and sixty-nine years after the time where I am to end this work
reign.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book V, p. 319 (facsimile PDF p. 415)
reign.note: A year in which Nebuchadnezzar was king. He does not say it is the accession. The 169 years measure how far this date falls after the end of the present volume.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 32; Menander of Ephesus, ap. Josephus
reign.note: In the reign of Ithobalus [or, Ethbaal]. The edition prints "beseiged". A footnote says Menander does not say the city was taken. No reign length is given for this Ithobalus.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 88; Berossus, ap. Alexander Polyhistor, ap. Eusebius
reign.note: First of two "43 years" on this page.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 88; Berossus, ap. Alexander Polyhistor, ap. Eusebius
reign.note: From Sinecherim to Nabucodrossorus. Our check, not a figure of the text beyond the 88: 18 + 8 + 21 + 21 + 20 = 88, using the reigns printed from Sennacherib through Nabopolassar and not Nebuchadnezzar's 43. The 88 matches that sum.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 88; Berossus, ap. Alexander Polyhistor, ap. Eusebius
reign.note: Second "43 years" on this page, in the captivity narrative. Same length as the list above.

reign.date: “our city was desolate during the interval of seventy years, until the days of Cyrus king of Persia”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 64; Berossus, ap. Josephus, Against Apion, book 1
reign.note: Josephus, Against Apion, book 1, chapter 19, as this page cites it. Nabopallasar sent Nabuchodonosor. No BC year is printed.
